svg.title: ithalat trackpad wiring (USB-C)
svg.desc: USB-C connector variant. The Azoteq TPS65 trackpad joins the Yakamoz OLED I2C1 bus (GP2/GP3). Four 30 AWG wires from tap A (OLED header joints or switchplate TB1) or tap B (Pico pins 4, 5, 36, 38) run flat over the switchplate, under the OLED cover, into the USB-C dock. There the 3V3 wire passes a series Schottky diode D1 (anode at the Pico, band toward the board) and the four wires reach the blue female USB-C breakout: G = GND, V = 3V3, D+ = SDA, D- = SCL. Both 5.1 kOhm CC resistors on the female are removed. The green male breakout in a printed grip mates with it and a short 4-wire lead goes to the TPS65 solder pads. No RDY. Not USB: never plug either half into a real USB port.
svg.text: ithalat trackpad wiring, USB-C: TPS65 on the OLED's I2C1 bus
4 wires, no RDY. Breakout pads: G = GND · V = 3V3 through Schottky D1 · D+ = SDA · D− = SCL
R1/R2: pull-ups on the main PCB (bottom side)
under the OLED cover → dock rear channel
No RDY wire: leave POINTING_DEVICE_MOTION_PIN undefined (default).
Tap B: or solder the four wires to Pico pins 4, 5, 36, 38
No case modification either way: only the OLED cover comes off.
in the dock's well · Rd × 2 removed
in the grip: shell epoxied, wires clamped
slack loop in the plug bay,
Tap A, top view: OLED header · TB1 socket
TB1: plug in a 5-pin male header, no soldering.
Not keyed: mark the GND end. Before power-up,
red must beep to Pico 36 and black to Pico 38.
same order below the OLED; acrylic bar must be filed.
Prepare the boards (top view, mouth up)
Female: remove both 5.1 kΩ Rd (marked 512 / 5101, or blank).
Male: remove any 56 kΩ (563) or 5.1 kΩ resistor.
Then CC → G reads open; shell → G usually beeps (may float).
thin line = PCB trace · thick line = wire
• NOT USB: never plug either half into real USB
• D1 in the 3V3 line, band toward the V pad
• Beep-test end to end, both plug orientations
• Hold the grip, steady the keyboard to plug in
• No breakaway: unplug before moving the rest
